newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen up slightly on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen up slightly on Friday.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell on Thursday but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main index up and analysts said the market should rise slightly on Friday but would maintain its current horizontal trend into next week.
Analysts said a rise was signalled by stronger buying after price fixing which might have been buoyed by the lower house of parliament's passing of less-inflationary 1997 tax legislation.

"The Sejm's (the lower house's) decision was not a surprise, we might have a rise to one percentage point but the decision's effect might only last until Friday," said Wojciech Smolka, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
The Sejm's previous tax bill before a Senate amemendment offered a steep tax cut for low earners.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.2 percent to 13,628.4 points and turnover fell 6.6 percent to 67.9 million zlotys ($24.1 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 44 to 21 with 18 stocks flat.

Analysts said biggest loser insurer Polisa, which plunged the maximum 10 percent the day after it had opened 12.5 percent above issue, was hurt by poor fundamentals versus the bourse's other insurer Warta, which was flat on Thursday.
Continuous trade turnover was at 0.9 million zlotys ($0.3 million) with four stocks up, one down and four flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 2.7 percent to 154 zlotys ($54.8) in the regular bourse session and rose 1.3 percent to 155 zlotys ($55.1) in continuous trade.

Turnover in both NFI sessions combined reached 87 million zlotys ($30.9 million), topping stock turnover, a signal which analysts said helped augur a continuation of the main market's horizontal trend.
They said small but numerous offers on the primary market this month would also keep stocks flat.
